metadata.note: The Kansas City, Clinton and Springfield Railway ('Leaky Roof', advertised as 'The Clinton Line'), Olathe KS - Belton - Harrisonville - Clinton - Osceola - Humansville - Ash Grove MO, 154.645 mi (ICC, 1917). Formed 1885 from the KCC&S Railroad and the Pleasant Hill & De Soto; Frisco stock control from 1901 but operated by its own organisation; absorbed by the Frisco (1924 operating takeover per one unverified item, 1928 deed per Killam & Alley) and run as its Osceola Subdivision; passengers last confirmed 1933; abandoned 1935, lifted 1936. Drawn as three KCC&S features (Olathe - Clinton 1885-1924; Clinton - Tracy Jct 1886-1917 [OPEN]; Tracy Jct - Ash Grove 1886-1924) and two Frisco features sharing the end sections' geometry (1924-1933 [OPEN]). The middle section has no Frisco-era feature: it was cut up piecemeal and partly absorbed into the Frisco High Line, whose trains belong on a separate (not yet drawn) Frisco High Line layer. Research report: research/branches/kansas_city_clinton_and_springfield_railway.txt.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (Overpass, maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-04): ways named 'Frisco RR Leaky Roof Line' with note:old_railway_operator=KCC&S
OpenHistoricalMap (2026-11-04): way -202707390 (Kansas City, Clinton and Springfield Railway, Harrisonville - Walnut Grove) and -202419410 (Pleasant Hill & De Soto line, Belton - Raymore)
metadata.operator_split: KCC&S to 1924, Frisco 1924-1933 on Olathe - Clinton and Tracy Jct - Ash Grove (Rule 4 split, identical geometry). 1924 is the report's recommended split and is UNVERIFIED; 1928 is the alternative.
not_yet_sourced: Frisco takeover of operation: 1924 (Springfield Republican item, seen only as a search snippet) vs 1928 (deed; Killam & Alley, Wikipedia, frrandp). The KCC&S/Frisco boundary at 1924 on all features is unverified; settle against a 1925-27 Official Guide or Frisco annual report.

OPEN END: kccs-clinton-tracy-jct ends 1917 = ICC valuation date, the last year the middle section is shown operated. When KCC&S passenger trains stopped running Clinton - Deepwater (lifted c.1926?) and Lowry City - Osceola - Harlan Jct (lift undated) is unknown.

OPEN END: frisco-osceola-sub-olathe-clinton and frisco-osceola-sub-tracy-jct-ash-grove end 1933 = last CONFIRMED year (two 1933 Official Guide station tags in Fowler). Secondary sources say 1934; ICC abandonment authority 1935; lifted 1936.
Start year: 1885 (Greene County, KC Star) vs April 1886 (ICC) - north end drawn from 1885, south of Clinton from 1886.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates; no KCC&S or Frisco Osceola Subdivision timetable was read.
Olathe - Stanley - Belton geometry is two straight chords (17.1 mi); the real alignment via Fort Scott Jct and Mastin is unmapped in OSM/OHM.
metadata.omitted: Report blocks 9-12 not drawn: Pleasant Hill branch (drawable NONE - no KCC&S passenger year confirmed); predecessor St. Louis, Lawrence & Denver / Santa Fe lease Cedar Jct - Olathe - Pleasant Hill (1875 anchor, operator unresolved); Cedar Jct - Olathe (owned, never operated by KCC&S, lifted 1894); KCFS&M/Frisco trackage Kansas City - Olathe and Ash Grove - Springfield (other roads' property). Freight-only remnants (Olathe - Stanley and Ash Grove - Phenix to c.1941-42, Harrisonville spur, Belton fragment) not drawn per Rule 1.

segments.note: KCC&S main line, north end (report block 1). Olathe - Stanley - Belton - Raymore was the 1871 St. Louis, Lawrence & Denver line bought with the Pleasant Hill & De Soto in 1885; Raymore Jct - Harrisonville - Clinton was new 1885 construction. First day of service Olathe - Clinton 27 July 1885 (Greene County release); KC Star 19 Nov 1885, quoted by Killam & Alley: 'This line has been in operation but a few weeks.' Conflict recorded: the ICC valuation says the PH&D section Olathe - Raymore Jct was 'placed in full operation April 1, 1886'. Run by the KCC&S's own organisation (ICC); Frisco stock control from 1901 did not change who ran the trains. Trains ran on to Kansas City over the KCFS&M (Frisco) from Olathe; that leg is not drawn here. Ridership peaked 1910-1919 at 'nearly 200,000 passengers a year'. The 1924 operator change follows a Springfield Republican item of 1924 (reported by the Springfield-Greene County Library; seen by the research only as a search snippet, the library page now 404s) saying the KCC&S 'lost its separate identity at midnight'. Killam & Alley (1953), Wikipedia and frrandp date the Frisco's taking deed to 1928. 1924 is used per CLAUDE.md Rule 4 (an operating takeover counts) but is UNVERIFIED; if 1928 proves right the KCC&S/Frisco boundary moves to 1928. Frisco stock control from 1901 (SHSMO: 1898) is not the split: the ICC valuation says the road was 'operated by its own organization during its entire life'. headway_min 1440 is an estimate from the Greene County release's 'once-daily passenger-and-freight service'; no KCC&S public timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: start 1885 from the Greene County release (27 Jul 1885) and the KC Star 19 Nov 1885 as quoted by Killam & Alley (ICC's April 1886 'full operation' conflict recorded in the note); end 1924 is the UNVERIFIED Frisco takeover date (1924 Springfield Republican item, snippet only), not a service end.

segments.note: KCC&S main line, middle (report blocks 3-6): Clinton - North Clinton - North's - Deepwater - Lowry City - Osceola (KCC&S Osage River bridge; it 'entered Osceola first' ahead of the Kansas City & Southern) - Harlan Jct - Vista - Tracy Jct. Start collapsed to 1886: Greene County says Ash Grove was reached Nov 1885, the ICC says Raymore Jct - Ash Grove was 'completed about April 1886'. Passenger service confirmed to 1917 by the ICC valuation (as of 30 June 1917), which records the whole 154.645-mi Olathe - Ash Grove main line owned and operated by the company with passenger equipment. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when KCC&S passenger trains stopped using this middle section. Afterwards: Clinton - Deepwater was torn up 'probably about 1926' (Killam & Alley), traffic then running over the High Line via Brownington; Lowry City - Osceola - Harlan Jct was lifted at an unrecorded date; Deepwater - Lowry City and Harlan Jct - Tracy Jct became part of the Frisco High Line, whose later trains belong on a Frisco High Line feature (not yet on the map), not here. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 1440 is an estimate from the Greene County release's 'once-daily passenger-and-freight service'; no KCC&S public timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: start 1886 from the ICC valuation ('completed about April 1886'; Greene County's Nov 1885 recorded as the earlier claim); end 1917 is the ICC valuation date, the last year a source shows the section operated - an OPEN end, not a known service end.

segments.note: Ex-KCC&S Olathe - Clinton (report block 2) run by the St. Louis-San Francisco as part of its Osceola Subdivision, Eastern Division (name per Killam & Alley). The 1924 operator change follows a Springfield Republican item of 1924 (reported by the Springfield-Greene County Library; seen by the research only as a search snippet, the library page now 404s) saying the KCC&S 'lost its separate identity at midnight'. Killam & Alley (1953), Wikipedia and frrandp date the Frisco's taking deed to 1928. 1924 is used per CLAUDE.md Rule 4 (an operating takeover counts) but is UNVERIFIED; if 1928 proves right the KCC&S/Frisco boundary moves to 1928. Frisco stock control from 1901 (SHSMO: 1898) is not the split: the ICC valuation says the road was 'operated by its own organization during its entire life'. Passenger service confirmed to 1933 by Fowler's Missouri list (line 108), which tags the KCC&S Clinton station 'South Clinton 1933G' from the 1933 Official Guide. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no primary source dates when service actually stopped (secondary sources say 1934; ICC abandonment authority 1935; track lifted 1936). The Olathe end in 1933 rests on the general 'Ash Grove and Olathe ... 1885 to 1934' statement. Do not extend without evidence. Afterlife, not drawn: Olathe - Stanley survived as a freight stub to c.1941-42 (Killam & Alley); a c.100-yd spur stayed at Harrisonville and a fragment survives at Belton. headway_min 1440 is an estimate: no Frisco Osceola Subdivision timetable was read, and Killam & Alley say the last service was a thrice-weekly mixed train (mixed trains count as passenger service).
